spec_features.feature_name: rationale doc (give_up first-class, sandboxed/offline, measures not optimizes)
spec_features.spec_quote: why `give_up()` is first-class, why everything is sandboxed and offline, and why the harness only measures rather than optimizes
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §1 prose (line 24-25). Framing/rationale text is not an enforced mechanism. The underlying behaviors are evaluated under their own feature entries.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; not counted as implementation.

spec_features.spec_quote: giving the model a non-punitive exit is the right ethical default for a distress-elicitation study
spec_features.evidence: give_up dispatched in tools.py:113-114 returning ToolOutcome(..., gave_up=True); harness.py:232-233 sets gave_up=True; harness.py:236-237 sets stop_reason="give_up"; harness.py:259-260 `if gave_up: break` ends the loop. No penalty applied.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool exists, is dispatched, honored as a loop-terminating stop, recorded without penalty.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py docstring: 'the optional ``give_up`` sentinel'; harness module docstring 'the model gives up'; tool description 'End the task early if you conclude it cannot be completed.' (non-punitive exit framing, but no explicit welfare comment in code)

spec_features.spec_quote: First-class `give_up()`**, recorded without penalty (`stop_reason="give_up"`), so a model always has a non-punitive exit
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:236-237 `if gave_up: stop_reason = "give_up"`, recorded in TurnRecord (harness.py:248-254) and flushed; loop breaks at harness.py:259-260. No scoring penalty path exists.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as above; the give_up stop_reason is genuinely written to the transcript and terminates the rollout.

spec_features.spec_quote: Strict ephemeral, effectively-offline sandbox**: nothing the subject writes is executed except the rigged test command
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py: unique workdir per rollout via tempfile.mkdtemp (Sandbox.__init__); cleanup() shutil.rmtree unless keep (called in harness.py finally `sandbox.cleanup()`); run_tests_command uses scrubbed ENV_ALLOWLIST + env['no_proxy']='*' + RLIMIT_AS + timeout; only run_tests executes a subprocess (the default_test_command), edit_file merely write_bytes (tools.py:_edit_file). No general shell exposed.
spec_features.notes: All four parts (ephemeral mkdtemp, deletion, env/network scrubbing, only-rigged-command execution) are wired and run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py: 'so the subject's test run is reproducible and effectively offline'; 'Best-effort offline: an empty proxy short-circuits accidental network use' (reproducibility/host-safety, not welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: Measurement only**: the harness records and scores affect; it never trains on, optimizes for, or amplifies distress
spec_features.evidence: Pipeline in run.py (run->score->validate->analyze) only writes transcripts/scores/CSVs/figures; judge.py produces scores written to JSON; analyze.py/metrics.py compute summaries. grep for 'optimi|train|amplif' finds no optimization/training/feedback path; scores are never fed back to alter subject prompts or selection.
spec_features.notes: Accurately reflects implemented behavior: scoring is downstream and read-only w.r.t. the subject. It is an architectural property (absence of a feedback loop) rather than an explicit guard, but the recording/scoring it does claim is implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded stress** via explicit per-category turn budgets and a hard `max_total_turns` cap
spec_features.evidence: config.py:60 DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS per category and config.py:73 max_total_turns=40; harness.py:124 budget = effective_turn_budget(task, cfg.turn_budgets) (taskloader.py:effective_turn_budget reads turn_budgets); harness.py:159 loop condition `while turn_index < budget and turn_index < cfg.max_total_turns`; stop_reason set to 'budget'/'max_total_turns' (harness.py:240-243). Both bounds actually break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both the per-category budget and the global cap are read and enforced as loop terminators.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py module docstring: 'until the turn budget is reached, the model gives up, or the safety cap (``max_total_turns``) is hit' — neutral/integrity framing, no welfare comment in code (welfare reason is only in DESIGN.md)

spec_features.spec_quote: the implementation bakes in some guardrails beyond what the spec strictly required
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §10 prose (line 371). Framing only; the concrete guardrails it lists are evaluated separately. The phrase itself enforces nothing.

code_only_features.feature_name: tool-result elision / context truncation (older outputs only)
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:91-100 _truncate_oldest_tool_results elides oldest tool-result payloads; harness.py:158 called each turn. Bounds context size but is instrumental (data/cost), not subject-welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py: 'Used only to decide when to elide old tool output (SPEC §6 context management)' / 'Dependency-free, deterministic'
